chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: 'Can the earth remain without an Imam?' He said: 'No.'

key_terms.إمام: Imam — the divinely appointed guide and authority from the Ahl al-Bayt, whose presence is held to be a cosmic necessity
key_terms.الأرض: The earth — referring not just to the physical world but to the inhabited human realm requiring divine guidance

ai.seo_question: Can the earth exist without an Imam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This brief but doctrinally weighty hadith records a direct question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether the earth could exist without a divinely appointed Imam. The Imam's unequivocal response — 'No' — reflects the Shia theological doctrine that the earth at all times requires a living hujja (divine proof). This teaching was particularly significant to early Shia communities who understood Imamate as the axis upon which the cosmic and social order turns.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the earth remain (existing) without an Imam<sup>asws</sup>: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-Husayn ibn abu ‘Ala’ from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Can the earth be without Imam?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “No, it can be without Imam.”
